So, this is going to be a little lengthy.

First let me say that as far as finance, I know that high credit is good, and that spending money is bad. That's it.

Longer story short, by the time I got out of the military, I had a credit score of around 600.

I had nowhere to go, so I lived with my mother. I've since moved out. Now, once I moved out, I needed a vehicle, and my mom wanted a different one. I tried to take over payment for her 2014 Cruze, and roughly 18,000 was too high for my credit so I got denied a vehicle loan.

Well, my mother's credit is terrible as well, and in order to get another loan (she has too many) she asked if I wanted to just pay her the Cruze's car note (350$) every month and she let's me keep it at my house and drive it around. Says once it's paid off, the title is mine (She's an incredible mom, I believe her, that's not the issue.)

Now, since she helped me out like that, I agreed to try for a loan for 3,000, for a used car she wanted. She pays directly into my account, every month.

So, neither title is in my name, but the 3,000$ loan is.

Now, she wants to trade in the car she has (payoff left is 2,000$) for a 9,000$ BMW, and try to get a 9,000$ loan in my name. How does this affect me credit-wise and financially? It sounds sketchy to me, but I have no knowledge of finances. Help please?
Loans, vehicles, family, and credit checks. I'm in a mess, and I need help.

How much do you still "owe" on the 2014 Cruze? i.e. could you take out a $9,000 loan to buy that from your mother, then let her go get her own loan and thus disentangle yourselves so you're each holding your own loans for your own vehicles?
I owe 16 on it, much too high for me to be able to get a loan so far, according to my credit union. So, pretty much just a waiting game.

Do you have a credit card? Getting one will greatly help you increase your score, and you won't have to pay any interest or fees to do it. I am happy to explain how if you're not clear on how this is done.

If you have a card, ask for a credit line increase. This will increase your credit score. You can usually ask for one ~every 6 months.

Paying those car loans is also helping your credit score assuming you are paying them on time.

Like the other guy said, taking loans out for someone else is usually considered a bad idea, but this isn't the life advice forum. However, personal finance-wise, it sounds like you and your mother can't afford this BMW, since you're trying to finance the entire cost of the vehicle. I think it would be more prudent to pay off the remaining $2,000, then sell that car to get the down payment for the next one. Or...do you two really need another car? She just got a Cruz that she couldn't afford and now doesn't want, so you had to take it over, and now she wants to ditch another car she got within the last 3-4 years max for a different expensive vehicle that she can't even afford a down payment for? If both cars work, think about what else you could be doing with that money - like saving to take care of your mother when she is older.
